hamlet-to-be.quote: “To be, or not to be, that is the question”
hamlet-to-be.blurb: A speech that sounds private, yet never once says “I”.

othello-trifles-proof.blurb: Iago knows that jealousy changes what counts as evidence.

macbeth-unsex-me-here.blurb: Lady Macbeth imagines resolve as a remaking of the body, but the command cannot settle what courage or cruelty will mean.

macbeth-is-this-a-dagger.quote: “Is this a dagger which I see before me”
macbeth-is-this-a-dagger.blurb: A question becomes a route towards murder as sight, touch and intention refuse to agree.

macbeth-tomorrow-and-tomorrow.blurb: Repetition makes time audible after the future Macbeth seized has emptied itself of purpose.

romeo-and-juliet-light.quote: “It is the east, and Juliet is the sun!”
romeo-and-juliet-light.blurb: Romeo praises an image that cannot hear him—until Juliet answers, and the play’s language changes.

king-lear-blow-winds.blurb: A king orders the storm to end mankind—and begins, for the first time, to describe himself truly.

tempest-our-revels.blurb: An interrupted masque becomes a speech in which the whole world dissolves like scenery.

doctor-faustus-thousand-ships.quote: “Was this the face that launch’d a thousand ships”
doctor-faustus-thousand-ships.blurb: The most famous praise of beauty in English drama is made entirely of burning things.

twelfth-night-food-of-love.quote: “If music be the food of love, play on”
twelfth-night-food-of-love.blurb: Orsino demands excess to cure his love—and disproves his own theory in four lines.

midsummer-nights-dream-imagination.small: A Midsummer Night’s Dream · Act 5, Scene 1
midsummer-nights-dream-imagination.quote: “The lunatic, the lover, and the poet”
midsummer-nights-dream-imagination.blurb: Theseus dismisses imagination from inside a fairy play; Hippolyta answers him in five lines.

richard-ii-sceptred-isle.quote: “This royal throne of kings, this sceptered isle”
richard-ii-sceptred-isle.blurb: Twenty lines of glory held in mid-sentence, waiting for a verb that arrives like a verdict.

henry-v-band-of-brothers.quote: “We few, we happy few, we band of brothers”
henry-v-band-of-brothers.blurb: A speech that admits the story will be improved in the telling—and works anyway.

merchant-of-venice-hath-not-a-jew-eyes.small: The Merchant of Venice · Act 3, Scene 1
merchant-of-venice-hath-not-a-jew-eyes.blurb: Remembered as a plea for tolerance; read whole, it ends in revenge and indicts its teachers.

duchess-of-malfi-still.small: The Duchess of Malfi · Act 4, Scene 2
duchess-of-malfi-still.blurb: Six words spoken in a cell, and four centuries of argument about what they claim.

richard-iii-winter-of-our-discontent.quote: “Now is the winter of our discontent”
richard-iii-winter-of-our-discontent.blurb: The villain opens the play alone, explains his body, and makes the audience his accomplice.

as-you-like-it-seven-ages.small: As You Like It · Act 2, Scene 7
as-you-like-it-seven-ages.blurb: Jaques’s seven ages—refuted a minute later by an old man carried on stage and fed.

measure-for-measure-to-die.quote: “Ay, but to die, and go we know not where”
measure-for-measure-to-die.blurb: Claudio imagines dying, in the body, and begs his sister for his life.

antony-and-cleopatra-the-barge.quote: “The barge she sat in, like a burnished throne”
antony-and-cleopatra-the-barge.blurb: The play’s cynic describes Cleopatra—and cannot stop.

sonnet-130-false-compare.quote: “My mistress’ eyes are nothing like the sun”
sonnet-130-false-compare.blurb: Twelve lines refuse every stock compliment; the couplet names the real target.

paradise-lost-mind-its-own-place.blurb: Satan claims the mind makes its own heaven—standing in Hell as he says it.

ancient-mariner-water-water.blurb: A ship painted on its own ocean, and thirst surrounded by sea.

tintern-abbey-sense-sublime.quote: “a sense sublime / Of something far more deeply interfused”
tintern-abbey-sense-sublime.blurb: Wordsworth audits what five years took from him, and what he would believe replaced it.

yeats-the-second-coming.quote: “Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold”
yeats-the-second-coming.blurb: Twenty-two lines that have supplied a century of titles, ending on a question.

aeneid-arms-and-the-man.blurb: Rome’s epic names its subject in three words and then asks why gods are cruel.

jekyll-duality.small: Jekyll and Hyde · Henry Jekyll’s statement
jekyll-duality.quote: “man is not truly one, but truly two”
jekyll-duality.blurb: A confident theory that begins to undo its own neat division.

douglass-pathway-freedom.blurb: An enslaver tries to forbid knowledge and accidentally reveals why it holds power.

jane-eyre-i-am-no-bird.quote: “I am no bird; and no net ensnares me”
jane-eyre-i-am-no-bird.blurb: A governess tells her employer that their souls stand equal—then refuses to be his bird.

yellow-wallpaper-got-out-at-last.blurb: The gentlest voice in the story gives the orders now.

dracula-children-of-the-night.quote: “the children of the night. What music they make!”
dracula-children-of-the-night.blurb: The Count says nothing untrue, and every courteous sentence lands twice.

robinson-crusoe-footprint.quote: “the print of a man’s naked foot on the shore”
robinson-crusoe-footprint.blurb: The castaway who prayed for company meets the evidence of it—and flees like one pursued.

woman-in-white-midnight-touch.quote: “the touch of a hand… from behind”
woman-in-white-midnight-touch.blurb: One of the first great thrillers begins with pure physical dread on an empty road.

moonstone-robinson-crusoe.quote: “such a book as Robinson Crusoe never was written”
moonstone-robinson-crusoe.blurb: The first great English detective novel opens not on a crime but on an old man and his favourite book.

werther-wonderful-serenity.quote: “A wonderful serenity has taken possession of my entire soul”
werther-wonderful-serenity.blurb: The happiest letter in the book already contains the whole tragedy.

pamela-dear-father-and-mother.quote: “Don’t wonder to see the paper so blotted”
pamela-dear-father-and-mother.blurb: A servant writes home; every reassurance is, for the reader, a warning.

sherlock-holmes-scandal.quote: “To Sherlock Holmes she is always the woman.”
sherlock-holmes-scandal.blurb: Before the case begins, Watson tells us who has already escaped Holmes’s categories.

moby-dick-call-me-ishmael.blurb: A famous opening gives us a name while holding the man behind it at a distance.

great-expectations-marsh-country.quote: “the small bundle of shivers … was Pip”
great-expectations-marsh-country.blurb: One long sentence names the world item by item and saves the frightened child for last.

scarlet-letter-rose-bush.blurb: A prison door, one flower at the threshold, and a narrator who refuses to decide.

war-of-the-worlds-opening.small: The War of the Worlds · Chapter 1
war-of-the-worlds-opening.blurb: The microscope turned around: mankind on the slide, and something at the eyepiece.

metamorphosis-vermin.blurb: A miracle stated as fact in the first sentence, and no one—least of all Gregor—is amazed.

mrs-dalloway-flowers-herself.blurb: An errand opens a door, and thirty years and a lost love come pouring through it.

ethan-frome-bit-by-bit.quote: “each time it was a different story”
ethan-frome-bit-by-bit.blurb: A narrator admits his sources disagreed, then describes a ruined man with total confidence.

tess-president-of-the-immortals.small: Tess of the d’Urbervilles · the last page
tess-president-of-the-immortals.blurb: Hardy ends with a black flag, two watchers and the most argumentative punctuation in Victorian fiction.

great-gatsby-boats-against-the-current.small: The Great Gatsby · the last page
great-gatsby-boats-against-the-current.quote: “So we beat on, boats against the current”
great-gatsby-boats-against-the-current.blurb: Nick widens one man’s ruined hope into a sentence about everyone still rowing.

the-fly-he-could-not-remember.quote: “For the life of him he could not remember”
the-fly-he-could-not-remember.blurb: Grief displaced onto a fly, discharged as torment, and then erased.

huckleberry-finn-apology.quote: “but I done it, and I warn’t ever sorry for it afterwards”
huckleberry-finn-apology.blurb: Huck’s plainest moral action arrives in the language society has given him.

pride-prejudice-self-knowledge.quote: “Till this moment I never knew myself.”
pride-prejudice-self-knowledge.blurb: Elizabeth’s revelation is earned by returning to the letter and reading against her own wishes.

frankenstein-adam.blurb: The creature uses the story of creation to turn origin into a claim about duty.

odyssey-olive-bed.blurb: Penelope trusts the private knowledge held in a bed made around a living tree.

christmas-carol-prisons.blurb: Scrooge turns a request for human help into a question about institutions.

uncle-toms-cabin-ice.blurb: Eliza crosses the Ohio on broken ice while the law pursues her child.

wuthering-heights-i-am-heathcliff.blurb: Catherine’s similes tighten, step by step, until only identity is left.

room-of-ones-own-money-and-a-room.small: A Room of One’s Own · Chapter One
room-of-ones-own-money-and-a-room.quote: “a woman must have money and a room of her own”
room-of-ones-own-money-and-a-room.blurb: A lecture that promises lies, cancels its speaker and proves its point by existing.

alice-in-wonderland-who-are-you.blurb: The rudest question in Wonderland is philosophy’s oldest—and the child’s answer is the rigorous one.

dorian-gray-preface.blurb: Aestheticism’s creed, written as a defence—and cross-examined by its own novel.

the-prince-feared-or-loved.blurb: The most notorious sentence in political thought, hedged on every side and built on one dark premise.

oroonoko-royal-slave.blurb: An early plea for a Black man’s humanity, caught in the racial arithmetic of its own age.

gullivers-travels-odious-vermin.quote: “the most pernicious race of little odious vermin”
gullivers-travels-odious-vermin.blurb: A giant king delivers the verdict Gulliver’s own boasting has earned.

iliad-hectors-helmet.blurb: The war poem stops at a gate: a baby screams at his father’s helmet, and everything is in the cry.

red-badge-sun-like-a-wafer.small: The Red Badge of Courage · Chapter IX
red-badge-sun-like-a-wafer.quote: “pasted in the sky like a wafer”
red-badge-sun-like-a-wafer.blurb: A friend dies, a soldier curses the world, and the sky answers with pure indifference.

call-of-the-wild-ecstasy.small: The Call of the Wild · Chapter III
call-of-the-wild-ecstasy.quote: “the ecstasy that marks the summit of life”
call-of-the-wild-ecstasy.blurb: London stops the hunt to argue that the peak of being alive is forgetting you are alive.

wind-in-the-willows-piper.small: The Wind in the Willows · Chapter VII
wind-in-the-willows-piper.blurb: Two small animals meet a god at dawn—and are given the gift of forgetting they ever did.

anne-of-green-gables-naming.small: Anne of Green Gables · Chapter II
anne-of-green-gables-naming.blurb: An orphan renames the world she was given too little of—and slowly the world agrees.

utopia-sheep-devour-men.quote: “your sheep… may be said now to devour men”
utopia-sheep-devour-men.blurb: More turns the mildest animal in England into a predator with a landlord behind it.

sense-and-sensibility-annuity.quote: “people always live for ever when there is an annuity”
sense-and-sensibility-annuity.blurb: Three thousand pounds talked down to nothing, and nobody lies.

henry-iv-what-is-honour.blurb: Falstaff takes the word apart in the form of a Sunday-school catechism, and wins the argument.

winters-tale-she-is-warm.blurb: A statue moves, and the play asks the audience to do what the king is asked: awake their faith.

much-ado-this-can-be-no-trick.small: Much Ado About Nothing · Act 2, Scene 3
much-ado-this-can-be-no-trick.blurb: It is a trick. Benedick reasons himself, clause by clause, from bachelor to lover.

coriolanus-i-banish-you.blurb: Sentenced to exile, Rome’s soldier turns the sentence round—and walks into his own destruction.

cymbeline-fear-no-more.quote: “Golden lads and girls all must, / As chimney-sweepers, come to dust”
cymbeline-fear-no-more.blurb: The most beautiful dirge in English, sung over someone who is not dead.

henry-vi-tigers-heart.quote: “O tiger’s heart wrapped in a woman’s hide!”
henry-vi-tigers-heart.blurb: The line a dying rival parodied in 1592 to call Shakespeare an upstart crow.

lucrece-times-glory.quote: “Time’s glory is to calm contending kings”
lucrece-times-glory.blurb: A woman with no listener puts Time on trial by listing everything it does.

king-john-grief-fills-the-room.quote: “Grief fills the room up of my absent child”
king-john-grief-fills-the-room.blurb: Two men tell a mother she is too fond of sorrow; her answer has outlived the play.

sign-of-four-seven-per-cent.small: The Sign of the Four · Chapter 1
sign-of-four-seven-per-cent.quote: “Which is it to-day, morphine or cocaine?”
sign-of-four-seven-per-cent.blurb: The second Holmes novel opens with a syringe, and Watson finally protests.

sleepy-hollow-ichabod-crane.quote: “The cognomen of Crane was not inapplicable”
sleepy-hollow-ichabod-crane.blurb: A schoolmaster built out of similes until he is a scarecrow you can see running.

man-who-was-thursday-victoria.small: The Man Who Was Thursday · Chapter I
man-who-was-thursday-victoria.quote: “he does say Victoria, and lo! it is Victoria”
man-who-was-thursday-victoria.blurb: The most poetic thing in the world, Syme argues, is a train arriving where the timetable said.

haunted-man-memory-green.blurb: Dickens ends his last Christmas book by saying nothing and letting a portrait speak.

henry-iv-part-2-uneasy-lies-the-head.small: Henry IV, Part 2 · Act III Scene 1
henry-iv-part-2-uneasy-lies-the-head.quote: “Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown”
henry-iv-part-2-uneasy-lies-the-head.blurb: A sleepless king asks why rest visits the ship-boy in a storm and not the man who wears the crown.

henry-viii-long-farewell.quote: “a long farewell to all my greatness”
henry-viii-long-farewell.blurb: Wolsey measures his fall in frost, blossom and a sea of glory that carried him beyond his depth.

troilus-and-cressida-degree.small: Troilus and Cressida · Act I Scene 3
troilus-and-cressida-degree.quote: “Take but degree away, untune that string”
troilus-and-cressida-degree.blurb: Ulysses argues that order is music and its loss appetite, a wolf that at last eats itself.

timon-of-athens-gold.small: Timon of Athens · Act IV Scene 3
timon-of-athens-gold.quote: “Thus much of this will make black white, foul fair”
timon-of-athens-gold.blurb: Digging for roots, Timon finds gold and lists the inversions money performs on everything it touches.

titus-andronicus-i-am-the-sea.quote: “I am the sea. Hark how her sighs doth flow!”
titus-andronicus-i-am-the-sea.blurb: Titus answers reasonable comfort by claiming grief the size of weather, sea against wind.

taming-of-the-shrew-thy-husband-is-thy-l.small: The Taming of the Shrew · Act V Scene 2
taming-of-the-shrew-thy-husband-is-thy-l.quote: “Thy husband is thy lord, thy life, thy keeper”
taming-of-the-shrew-thy-husband-is-thy-l.blurb: Katherina’s last speech wins the wager and starts four centuries of argument about whether she means it.

comedy-of-errors-drop-of-water.small: The Comedy of Errors · Act I Scene 2
comedy-of-errors-drop-of-water.quote: “I to the world am like a drop of water”
comedy-of-errors-drop-of-water.blurb: Before the farce accelerates, Antipholus states its cost: a self that could dissolve while searching for its match.

loves-labours-lost-womens-eyes.small: Love’s Labour’s Lost · Act IV Scene 3
loves-labours-lost-womens-eyes.quote: “From women’s eyes this doctrine I derive”
loves-labours-lost-womens-eyes.blurb: Berowne turns a broken oath into philosophy, and the play lets the argument dazzle without letting it win.

alls-well-our-remedies.small: All’s Well That Ends Well · Act I Scene 1
alls-well-our-remedies.quote: “Our remedies oft in ourselves do lie”
alls-well-our-remedies.blurb: Helena stops mourning her distance from Bertram and decides the fated sky gives her free scope.

two-gentlemen-launce-and-crab.small: The Two Gentlemen of Verona · Act II Scene 3
two-gentlemen-launce-and-crab.blurb: Launce restages his family’s farewell with shoes, a staff and a dog who refuses to shed a tear.

venus-and-adonis-purple-coloured-face.quote: “Hunting he lov’d, but love he laugh’d to scorn”
venus-and-adonis-purple-coloured-face.blurb: The poem that made Shakespeare famous opens with the goddess of love as a bold-faced suitor.

cricket-on-the-hearth-the-kettle-began-i.small: The Cricket on the Hearth · Chirp the First
cricket-on-the-hearth-the-kettle-began-i.blurb: Dickens opens his third Christmas book with a narrator arguing about who sang first, kettle or cricket.
